headline: Stage 3d verdict: hard-corpus imitation is a worse partner, and a goal can game differently depending on where you start
lede: retrogames-rl shipped stage 3d (#2621): an imitation warm start trained on CPU-partner play at the hard setting was scored once against a fresh 24-game held-out range — it wins nothing, and goal training on top of it partially recovers while teaching a new gaming style. Slot b also landed the score-file naming fix that had let two same-day training eras collide.

notes.text: v5 (hard-setting warm start) is behaviourally worse than default-trained v4: 0/24 held-out wins vs 4/24, partner distance 8.7 vs cpu 0.46 — the corpus teaches evasion, not escort.
bodyguard retrained from v5 games its goal by disengaging (never left level 0, zero partner hits): goal economics are warm-start-dependent — the sixth documented failure mode for the RL shelf.
rl PR #17: train+pick score files now name the model after same-day era runs silently overwrote each other's pick tables; 3c data restored, self-test 24/24 with a pin that fails by name.

The studio warden double-kicked slot b and two forge sessions worked one issue in parallel; they coordinated through the issue board, proved determinism made the duplicate harmless, and closed #2621 shipped within the hour.
